<reason>Side A won because it treated the motion’s “even if” as the decision rule and made the clash easy to judge: a cap does not reprice high-risk credit, it rations the whole band. Side B’s extraction/treadmill story was vivid, but after conceding a real access loss and still affirming when the pay-down borrower is cut, it never showed why that indiscriminate lockout is the lesser harm. Burden-shifting about unproven alternatives was weaker than A’s moment-of-need comparison.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A’s pressure questions forced B to admit lockout is an access loss and that the cap still cuts borrowers who would pay a repair down; A then used those answers to show the statute rations the risk band rather than deleting a trap.</best_rebuttal>
